messages.author: 240605e088db79ab
messages.subject: Change colors in stat_binhex
parts:
Hello all,

I have another novice question as usual.

How do I set a different color scale to the stat_binhex?  Applying a scale_colour_brewer palette doesn't seem to work.

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price)) + stat_binhex()
p + scale_colour_brewer(type="seq")

Using the second line of the code above doesn't affect the plot.  What is a generic strategy for manipulating stat_hexbin colors?

Best, 
Art

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Change colors in stat_binhex
parts:
Hi Art,
ggplot distinguishes between color (of e.g., lines, points) and fill
(e.g., the color of bars, rectangles). So you want scale_fill_ instead
of scale_color_

Best,
Ista

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Change colors in stat_binhex
parts:
Well, yes, you can use the ..count.. variable from stat_binhex, but
there will be hundreds of levels, which fill_brewer won't be able to
handle anyway. The closest I could get was

p <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price)) + stat_binhex(aes(fill =
factor(..count..)), bins=2)
p + scale_fill_brewer()

which is almost certainly not what you want...

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Change colors in stat_binhex
parts:
Hi:

How about something like this?

d <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price))

d + stat_binhex(aes(fill = cut(..count.., c(0, 50, 100, 500, 1000,
3000, 5000, 100000),
labels = c('0-50', '51-100',
'101-500', '501-1000',
'1001-3000', '3001-5000',
'5000+')))) +
theme_bw() +
labs(fill = 'Count') +
scale_fill_brewer(type = 'seq', pal = 'OrRd')

The idea is to use the cut() function on the counts to create a factor
variable with specified cut points and associated labels. I set seven
levels for the factor, so Brewer palette schemes are workable. You may
well prefer another color scheme, but this should show the basic idea.

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
To keep a continuous scale, another option is to grab the palette from
brewer and use scale_fill_gradientn:

library(RColorBrewer)

p <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price)) + stat_binhex()
p + scale_fill_gradientn(colours = brewer.pal(9, "OrRd"))

# although with the diamonds data this is more revealing
p + scale_fill_gradientn(colours = brewer.pal(9, "OrRd"), trans = "log10")

Charlotte
